chunks: And from him, from Abd al-Rahman, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The patient who is overcome (by illness) and the one who is unconscious, circumambulation is performed on their behalf.

key_terms.وَالْمُغْمَى عَلَيْهِ: And the one who is unconscious
key_terms.وَيُطَافُ بِهِ: And circumambulation is performed for them
key_terms.يُرْمَى عَنْهُ: Is thrown/positioned on their behalf (referring to the representative standing in their place)

ai.seo_question: How is circumambulation performed for a sick or unconscious person in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), establishing the permissibility of *tawaf al-wada'* or *tawaf al-ziyarah* being performed by a proxy for those incapacitated by severe illness or unconsciousness. This ruling highlights the flexibility of Shia jurisprudence in accommodating physical limitations while maintaining the spiritual obligation of circumambulating the Kaaba. It underscores the principle that the intent (*niyyah*) and the act of the representative suffice when the individual is unable to perform the ritual themselves.
